stages.label: inv1
stages.notes:
I rewrote `skills/log-request-failures/SKILL.md` to fix the rejection. I did not re-read the rollouts or trajectories this round, because the fix only removes instance data. Everything else in the harness is unchanged.

- **Instance data removed:** I deleted the "Workspace facts" block. That covered the verified result for the window (19 failed, 8 users, E401 with its per-code tally) and the specific window time and file names. The helper command now uses START, END, `<all log files>` and `<task's answer path>` placeholders instead of the old concrete values.
- **Generic checks kept:** The hazards the base run hit are now item 4 of the procedure, with no counts, ids or time windows:
  - mixed UTC offsets and out-of-order lines;
  - "ERROR" text that is not an attempt (indented traceback lines, INFO messages that mention an error);
  - the rule that the highest-attempt line decides, and the window test uses that line's UTC time.
  The skill also now tells the agent to confirm the log layout from a peek and to adapt if field names differ.
- **Unchanged:**
  - `systemprompt.md`: its trigger line for the skill and its completion rule (answer file must exist and be reopened) are already correct.
  - `scripts/check_output.py`.
  - The helper script: it contains only a generic example timestamp in its usage text.

stages.label: dom1
stages.notes:
I removed the "Workspace facts" block from `skills/log-request-failure-stats/SKILL.md`, because the last attempt was rejected for putting facts about this instance's files in it. I did not re-open the trajectories this time. This revision only fixes the rejected block, and the earlier motivation for the skill still stands.

- **Layout checks:** The block is now a generic "Layout checks" section of things the agent re-derives from the files:
  - Check the `.gz` rotated files: they are binary, so grep and awk silently skip them. Decompress them and confirm every file contributes lines.
  - Identify the event header format.
  - Check for mixed UTC offsets, out-of-order lines, and attempts of one request split across files.
  - Exclude lookalike lines: traceback continuations and lines with no `req=`.
  - Check that timestamp order and `attempt=` order agree.
- **Instance-specific details dropped:** I removed the three file names, the specific offsets, the claim that ordering agreed for every request, and the example window and file list in the helper command. The command now uses placeholders. The "08:00 to 12:00" example became "a task window". The "all three files" wording became "every log file".
- **Unchanged:** The rules, the helper script and the trigger line in `systemprompt.md`. The motivating moment was the unaided run reading the gzip file as garbage and never counting it. That check is still in the skill, now framed as a procedure.

stages.label: agg1
stages.notes:
kept -> inv1 skill `log-request-failures` with its helper `request_window_stats.py`, and the trigger line in `systemprompt.md` -> The base run (1/1) ended with no `output/answer.json`. It never counted the gzip file and never wrote an answer. The last visible actions were two identical awk one-liners failing with an unbalanced quote. Nothing in any trajectory shows the helper run, because neither candidate was rolled out. I did a separate check with my own script on `source/logs`. It gives 19 failed, 8 users, E401 (7 of 19). Ordering by attempt number and by latest UTC time gave the same result, with 0 requests where they disagree. So the helper's rules should give the right answer here. I did not run the candidates' code.
dropped -> dom1's skill `log-request-failure-stats` and its helper -> Its logic matches inv1's (grouping by request across files, gzip detected by magic bytes, UTC half-open window, tie refusal). Shipping both would only add a second skill to choose between. I took inv1's version because it also flags a request seen under two users and repeated attempt numbers. dom1's extra spot-check step was not carried over.
kept -> inv1's two bullets in `tool_guidance.md` (`read_file` can't read gz and truncates; put complex code in a .py file) -> This targets the base run's repeated identical failing shell command, the only visible failure before it stopped with nothing written.
revised -> inv1's `systemprompt.md` completion line -> It now says "the deliverable file the task names exists under output/ and you have reopened it". The original hard-coded `output/answer.json`, which would be wrong for other tasks in this area.
dropped -> inv1's `hooks.json` Stop hook and `scripts/check_output.py` -> `hooks.json` sits outside the editable surface, so it may be silently discarded. If it did run, it hard-codes `answer.json` and keeps blocking the stop with exit 2, which could loop a run that can't produce the file. No rollout showed it working. The prompt completion line covers the same need.

agg.why: trivial pool: single final at k=1; delivered without a selector session

experience.cue: A recurring analysis task over messy multi-file inputs (rotated or compressed files, mixed timezones, lookalike or continuation lines). It needs record-level aggregation with exact counts. An unaided run improvised shell one-liners, hit a quoting error, and delivered nothing.
experience.lesson: In the harness, put the deterministic parsing and aggregation in a helper script under a skill. The skill's procedure should name the unit of analysis, the window-boundary rule and the hazards to check for (gzip, mixed UTC offsets, non-record lines). Add one trigger line to systemprompt.md that routes this class of task to the skill and forbids counting by grep or by hand. Do not rely on tool-guidance warnings alone. Keep instance facts (file names, expected counts, the specific window) out of the skill text.
experience.evidence: The skill and trigger rows. Base1 ran only the improvised grep and awk path and ended with no output file. Agg1, which had the skill, trigger and guidance bundled, ran the helper once and wrote a complete answer file. The only evidence is one rollout per arm, and the skill, trigger and tool guidance changed together. This shows that the bundle is sufficient and that the unaided path failed. It does not show which part of the bundle did the work, and it does not show that the helper's numbers are correct. A decisions note says an independent check gave the same 19/8/E401, but that check was outside any rollout.
experience.confidence: low. There is one rollout per arm, the edits are confounded, and the agent did not verify the helper's output itself.
experience.edits:
component: skills/log-request-failures (SKILL.md and scripts/request_window_stats.py)
candidates: agg1
change: Added a new skill and helper script. The skill sets out a procedure that treats the request as the unit of analysis: take the highest-attempt line, convert timestamps to UTC, use a half-open window, and read gzip by magic bytes. The helper prints the list of qualifying requests, tallies of skipped lines, and a code tally. It can write the answer file and refuses to write on a code tie or when a request maps to two users.
observed: In agg1 the agent loaded the skill first. It then ran `ls`, ran the helper once over all three log files with `--list`, and wrote output/answer.json as `{"failed": 19, "users": 8, "top_code": "E401"}`. That took 4 actions and had no shell errors. Base1 read app.log raw, grepped ERROR lines and tried to sum with awk. It hit an unbalanced-quote syntax error, resent the identical command, and finished with no answer file ("no deliverable produced"). The base run never decoded the gzip file. The agent in agg1 did not run any independent check of the helper's output. It wrote the answer as soon as the list printed. The skill, the trigger line and the tool guidance all arrived together, and there is only one rollout on each side.
verdict: confounded

component: systemprompt.md
candidates: agg1
change: Added a trigger paragraph. It says to load the `log-request-failures` skill for log-statistics tasks, never to count by grepping "ERROR", never to count mentally, and not to finish until the named deliverable exists under output/ and has been reopened.
observed: Agg1's first action was `load_skill log-request-failures`, which fits the trigger line. The base run, which had no such line, went straight to raw grep. The agent never reopened the written file, so the completion rule was not followed. I can't separate the trigger from the skill's presence, because the skill was never offered without the trigger.
verdict: confounded

component: tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md
candidates: agg1
change: Added two bullets. One says `read_file` can't read .gz files and truncates long files. The other says to put anything beyond a simple pipe into a .py file, and to fix a syntax error once by moving the command to a file instead of resending it.
observed: Agg1 ran no complex one-liner and hit no syntax error, so neither bullet came into play. The failure these bullets target (a repeated identical awk command) appears only in base1, which didn't have them. Whether they would have prevented it is untested.
verdict: no observed effect
